chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of speaking at the meeting of the two circumcised parts (penis and anus), for it causes dumbness.'

key_terms.الْخِتَانَيْنِ: The two circumcised parts, referring to the penis and the anus.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of avoiding speech during defecation in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises avoiding speech during the act of defecation, specifically when the penis and anus meet, stating that this practice leads to dumbness (khuras). This narration is often interpreted by Shia scholars as referring to both physical ailments affecting the vocal cords and spiritual consequences, such as the loss of eloquence in conveying divine wisdom, reflecting the holistic view of the body and soul in Shia tradition.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Qasim, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Beware of the speaking during the meeting of the two private parts, for it inherits the dumbness’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from a man from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “About the case of a man who looks at his wife when she is nude,
abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is not unlawful. Pleasure is but in such things.’”
